title: Conveyor Permit Route
primary_skill: Run BFS over position plus remaining permit state.
interview_signal: Candidate can recognize that reaching the same station with a different permit count can change future reachability.
description_md: A warehouse has numbered stations connected by one-way conveyor links. Each link is represented as [from, to, permit_delta]. Moving across a link always takes one step. A negative permit_delta consumes permits, while a positive permit_delta restores permits up to a fixed cap. Return the fewest steps from start to target without ever dropping below zero permits, or -1 if the target cannot be reached.

examples.explanation: The route through station 2 reaches station 1 with more permits available, allowing the final restricted conveyor.

constraints: Each link is [from, to, permit_delta] with valid station indices.

starter_code.python:
def fewest_conveyor_steps(station_count: int, links: list[list[int]], start: int, target: int, permits: int, permit_cap: int) -> int:
    pass

canonical_solution_md: Use breadth-first search because every conveyor traversal has the same step cost. The state must include both the current station and current permit count. For each outgoing link, compute the next permit count after applying the link delta, discard moves that would go below zero, and cap restored permits at the maximum. A station reached with more permits can enable different future moves, so visited tracking must include the permit count. The first time the target state is reached gives the fewest steps.
fallback_hints: Think about whether being at a station is enough information to know what moves are still possible.
The same station can be more useful when reached with more permits available.
Use a shortest-path search over station and permit count together, and ignore transitions that would make permits negative.
common_mistakes: Marking only stations as visited and throwing away a later state with more permits.
Letting restored permits exceed the permit cap.
Using depth-first search and assuming the first route found is shortest.
Treating one-way conveyor links as bidirectional.
follow_up_questions: How would the approach change if conveyors had different traversal times?
How would you reconstruct the actual route instead of only the step count?
What changes if permit restoration only happens once per station?

suboptimal_solutions.name: DFS over all routes
suboptimal_solutions.description: Explores many repeated states and does not naturally guarantee the fewest steps.

suboptimal_solutions.name: BFS with station-only visited
suboptimal_solutions.description: Can discard a later visit to the same station that has more permits and is necessary for a valid route.
